# Badge

A short label for a status, category or count, next to what it describes.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** A status label with an icon and a word, in a clear rectangle. Not color alone, and not a pill.

- **Use it when:** A state people scan for in a list or table, or a small category label.
- **Not when:** A message people must read (alert or toast), or an action (a button).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): A message, not a label.
- [Button](./button.md): Something to press.

## Why it works this way

Badge looks the way it does because of 5 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Badge, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many signals carry each meaning?</b><code>accessibility.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Three: color, icon and word</div><p>Never color alone.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Badge</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: A waiting state, such as an application saved to resume later, with an icon and a word.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>success</b>: A finished task, with a filled icon and a word.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>warning</b>: A risk people can still fix before they finish, with an icon and a word.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: A failure that blocks the task, with a filled icon and a word; an alert says how to fix it.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">4</div><small>Badge decisions would reopen</small><p>and 1 answer that follow from it: <b>Status and messages</b>.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-scenarios-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How long is one visit?</b><code>scenarios.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One sitting</div><p>An application is finished in one sitting, or saved and resumed.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Badge</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: A waiting state, such as an application saved to resume later, with an icon and a word.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Badge decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The status is a word; color and icon add to it, never replace it. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add badge
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Component keys

The CSS variable is the key with `/` replaced by `-` and the base `@` dropped. Each key points to a token; values live only on primitives.

| Key | What it controls | Points to, light | Points to, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `badge/radius` | Badge corner radius. | `radius.badge` → `accessible-first.theme.base.radius.badge` → `radius.4` | same |
| `badge/padding-x` | Horizontal padding inside a badge. | `space.gap.tight` → `space.12` | same |
| `badge/font-size` | Badge label size. | `type.caption.font-size` → `font.size.16` | same |
| `badge/neutral/background` | Neutral badge fill. | `color.surface.sunken` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.surface.sunken` → `color.gray.light.100` | `color.surface.sunken` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.surface.sunken` → `color.gray.dark.100` |
